answer: A comet of scarce licensed spectrum anchors each agent’s identity to a registered cell, so a sybil swarm must acquire distinct physical placements rather than spin up keys. Each thread of uplink budget is link-budgeted against interference: agents in the same sector share a capacity ceiling, making mass fake identities degrade the attacker’s own signal-to-noise margin. The pearl is a per-cell admission cap enforced by RF planning, costing an attacker real spectrum leases and site fees per identity, though dense urban reuse limits how finely cells can separate colluding sybils.
